summary: Marco Walther works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He completed his PhD at the University of Munich under the doctoral supervision of Franz-Karl Ehrhard.

Marcus Bingenheimer specializes in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and computational fields. He studied at Nagoya University under Yasuhisa Matsumura and at the University of Würzburg, later holding posts at Chung-Hwa Institute, Dharma Drum institutions, and Temple University (2012–2015).

Marek Mejor is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He held a Junior Research Fellowship at Wolfson College, Oxford (1981–1982) and was a professor at the University of Warsaw (attested 2000–2010).

Marek Zemánek works in religious and Buddhist studies. He studied at Seoul National University, Dongguk University, and Charles University, where he completed his dissertation under the supervision of Radek Chlup.
Marek Zvelebil (1952–2011) was a scholar in history and archaeology. He studied at the University of Sheffield and held an academic post there from circa 1987 to 2011.
Margaret Gouin is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She completed her PhD at the University of Bristol under the doctoral supervision of Paul Williams.

Margaret H. Dornish specializes in religious and Buddhist studies. She studied at Yale, Claremont Graduate University, and the University of Southern California, and served as Associate Professor of Religion at Pomona College (attested 1989).

Margaret Mead (1901–1978) studied at Barnard and Columbia under Franz Boas. She held long-term posts at the American Museum of Natural History, Columbia University, The New School, and Fordham, and founded the Institute for Intercultural Studies.

Margaret R. Miles is a scholar of religious studies and history. After earning her PhD from the Graduate Theological Union, she taught at Harvard Divinity School (~1978–1996) and returned to GTU as dean (1996–2001).

Margarita Angelica Delgado Creamer specializes in religious studies and Sinology. She completed her PhD at the University of Pittsburgh under supervisor Linda Penkower and also studied under postdoctoral mentor Xiuping Hong.

Margarita Iosifovna Vorobyova-Desyatovskaya was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist, and Iranian/Central Asian studies. Educated at Saint Petersburg State University, she held long-term positions at the Institute of Oriental Studies and the Institute of Oriental Manuscripts.
Margarita Kleibel is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied under MA supervisor Klaus-Dieter Mathes and teacher Karin Preisendanz.

Maria Heim works in Buddhist and religious studies. She studied at Reed College and earned her PhD at Harvard University under Charles Hallisey, later serving as Associate Professor of Buddhist Studies at Amherst College (attested 2013–2020).

Maria Krzysztof Byrski is an Indology scholar who studied at the University of Warsaw (~1955–1960). He later served as Head of the Indology Department at the University of Warsaw (~1990–1996) and held a post at Civitas University.

Marian Ury (1932–1995) was a scholar in Japanology and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD from the University of California, Berkeley, and served as professor of East Asian languages and comparative literature at UC Davis (1969–1995).

Marianne Pieper studied at HWP and Otto von Guericke University Magdeburg. She held academic posts at the University of Kassel (1994–1996) and served as a professor of sociology at the University of Hamburg (1996–2015).

Marianne Winder (1918–2001) studied at London, Nottingham, UCL, and SOAS under David Snellgrove. A specialist in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, she served as Assistant Librarian and Curator at the Wellcome Institute for the History of Medicine.
Marie G. Wanek is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. She studied at the University of Pennsylvania, where she was taught by Sengaku Mayeda.

Marielle Harrison specializes in religious and Buddhist studies. A doctoral student at the University of Chicago, she is attested in 2026 as an HCBSS Postdoctoral Fellow Lecturer at Stanford University.
Marina Illich is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She completed her PhD at Columbia University in 2006 under the supervision of Robert A. F. Thurman.
